title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 15
text: Well, the chocolates labeled “Filo’s Handmade Chocolates” have already been delivered. They’re scheduled to be handed out at the venue entrance as soon as the doors open, in exchange for vouchers. After that, Filo’s live performance will begin. I leave the sales booth in Raphtalia’s care, move to a spot with a good view, and peer down at the venue entrance.

Keel’s setup is pretty much the same. However, since Keel’s setup isn’t very visible, I watch the crowd waiting for Keel’s chocolate from above the venue. Since they’ve set up separate entrances, it’s easy to tell them apart.

Huh? Keel’s side has a decent crowd showing up, too. The age group… is different from Filo’s. It’s full of adult women and kids. I guess Keel’s chocolate was a flop after all. I had them make it to the same specifications as Filo’s. We should’ve gone with chocolate cookies or something like that.
“Hey. Are we there yet?”
A child at the front of the line is waiting for the doors to open with her mother.
“Just a little longer.”
“I’m so excited for Keel-kun’s event!”
“Yeah… I wonder what that innocent Keel-kun will do for us.”
“I gave him some jerky the other day. Keel-kun was so cute!”

That’s when a new idea suddenly pops into my head. It’ll definitely sell in a different way than Filo! In Keel’s case, something girls would love… like a plushie of Keel in his dog form. I’ll have them make that. It’s sure to sell. Just as I was thinking that, it was time for the doors to open.
“Please don’t rush in. As long as you have your ticket, you can exchange it, so please don’t rush in.”
It reminds me of when I was in Japan. I wasn’t an idol otaku, so I’d never actually gone to an idol event, but I had been to doujin conventions. This feels a bit like that.

If I remember correctly, the exchange tickets for Keel sold out in half a day after they went on sale. As for Filo’s, they sold out within an hour of going on sale—probably because Motoyasu bought them all up. Just how popular are they, anyway? Still, it’s surprising how different the types of customers are.

Maybe it’s better this time since it’s not handshake tickets or anything like that. Melty also mentioned that when handshake tickets go on sale, Filo sometimes acts like she hates it, so it’s a pain to calm her down. Do people really want to shake Filo’s hand that badly…? Not that I’m the best person to say this, since I was the one who suggested it. How about gathering 48 Filolials and having them perform as idols? They’re all pretty much the same, though… I doubt we could differentiate their characters. They’re not exactly the brightest, so managing them would be tough. Just as I thought.
“Thanks, everyone!”
Oh? Has the show started over on Filo’s side? I hear cheers, so I head over through the staff passageway to check it out. The lighting—invented by Trash—is shining on Filo.
I’m speechless at the sight of the packed venue. It’s even bigger than when I first went off the rails. Filo’s holding a mic and has started singing. She’s already hyped up right from the start.

I had new outfits prepared for Filo specifically for this event. I think the theme this time was Valentine’s Day. She’s wearing an outfit with a wrapping-paper-like pattern and has a ribbon tied around her hair. Filo really loves to sing, after all. Melty is also playing an instrument in the back.

Now that Melty has become a “Hero of Instruments,” she can provide some support to the crowd through her music. I bet what Melty is playing right now is a modified version of one of her Skills. Filo sings, dances, and strikes poses. With explosions going off in the background, the venue is really heating up.
“Filo-taaan! Go for it!”
Motoyasu is giving instructions to the fan club, making them create waves and project letters into the air. They’re a lively bunch.
“We’re not losing today!”
“‘Ooh! The Triples have barged in!’”

That’s a weird team name. It looks like the Three-Color Filolial Reals have barged in, and it’s turned into a singing battle. Filo and the gang are as reliable as ever. They’re not going to mess this up. The chocolate side had a 90% exchange rate, too. It’s practically sold out. As for the remaining 10%… I don’t know what happened there—it’s outside my jurisdiction.
So… let’s check Keel’s side. Oh!? Keel’s exchange rate is slightly higher. It’s 92%. I head over to Keel’s venue.
“Uh, um… ‘You all set me up, didn’t you? I won’t lose to a conspiracy!’”

I hadn’t been involved in planning the performance at all, so I don’t know the details. I thought Raphtalia was supervising it—what on earth is she doing? There’s Keel, dressed in a loose-fitting cloth outfit, holding a pot lid and putting on a play. She looks pretty inexperienced and seems a bit embarrassed. Still, the audience is cheering her on with kind eyes, saying, “Go for it!” and Keel seems to be gradually relaxing and getting into the swing of things.
“‘This country uses slaves, doesn’t it? Why do I have to be the only one confiscated?’… Is that right?”

Ugh… this is just a kids’ play. Under the stage, Imiya is holding up a cue card. She hasn’t memorized her lines yet… They really should make her rehearse properly. Is that too difficult given Keel’s personality? Actually, something’s been bothering me for a while now… Could it be?
“Rafu!”

A slave playing a soldier is, for some reason, grabbing Raph-chan, who’s playing the heroine. Raph-chan has a dagger tucked at her waist and is whimpering. Raph-chan’s acting is actually better. Even though she’s only whimpering “Rafu,” it’s as if her lines are coming through clearly. Just to clarify, the narrator is voicing Raph-chan’s lines for us.
So… why the hell is that Trash playing the king over here? Are you here to help Melty with her work? Go handle your official duties at the castle! Just how into this is he?
“‘In this country, what I say is law! If you don’t obey, I’ll confiscate your slaves by force!’”
I can hear boos. Wait… did he actually say that? I can’t even laugh at this. But that’s all part of the act—Keel gets so excited he turns into a puppy, causing the audience to burst into laughter.
“‘Then I’ll hold a duel in the castle courtyard!’”
No doubt about it! This… isn’t this a play based on me?! I look at the poster plastered on the venue on Keel’s side.
The title is *The Legend of the Shield Hero*, Act One… Hey!

Is Keel playing my role?! I did say I wanted to play a male role, but why do I have to watch a play based on a story modeled after me? The play continued until the part where Raphtalia, even after being freed from slavery, said she’d stay with me, and then Act I ended.
“The Shield Hero must’ve had it rough—Keel-kun was so cute.”
“That’s right. The Shield Hero saved this world.”

Just when I thought it was finally over, another play began. Next up… a story about a princess dressed as a man who sets the world right. Partway through the story, she seemed to fall under a curse and transform.
“‘Ugh… the curse has turned me into a wolf…’ Woof woof!”

Keel transforms into his Cerberus form and runs around the theater. In the end, the villain who cast the curse is defeated—a happy ending? Afterward, everyone involved in the play gathers together to take their bows.
“Thank you so much for coming today—”
Keel stumbled over his words. But the audience was forgiving, and laughter welled up.
“Go, Keel-kun! Do it again next time!”
With that, chocolates were thrown into the auditorium as a token of appreciation.
“Thanks!”
“Keel-kun, over here!”
“Woof woof!”
Perhaps because they were sweets, Keel transformed into his Cerberus form and began devouring them.
“Huh? Why does the chocolate smell like me?”

Whoa!? Did that guy Keel notice!? But Keel just tilted his head; he didn’t seem to think anything of it beyond that and was waving his hand. The audience watched the scene with amusement. It was a scene where I couldn’t tell if it was just peaceful or if it had its own unique vibe. And just like that, the two Valentine’s Day events ended on a huge high note.
I left the cleanup of the venue to Raphtalia and hurried back to the village. The sun had set, and night was falling. I’d better get dinner ready…

Zeltoble had offered to handle the cleanup and the celebratory toast afterward, so Raphtalia and Keel would be staying over there. I’ve got my own work to do here—I need to plan for the traveling trade and the next event. I’m sure there’ll be a Doll Festival coming up, too. Better safe than sorry.
Oh? Looks like Ren and the others have returned via the portal. Ren, looking a bit restless, is talking with the female knight and Taniko.
“See you later, Ren. We’ve got an early start tomorrow, so get some rest.”
“…Good night.”
“O-oh…”

You should notice that Ren is holding both hands out slightly in front of him. He definitely didn’t make any chocolate. Or maybe he noticed but is just playing it off? Hmph… I actually went out of my way to be considerate of that pitiful Ren, you know?

Ren noticed that there were chocolates in the mailbox in front of his house. Well, up to that point, he’d probably just assume they were obligatory chocolates from the villagers. But when he spotted a box of chocolates inside with rough, clumsy wrapping, Ren’s eyes widened. There were also some with dragon designs on the packaging. After checking the contents, Ren flashed a smirk at the female knight and Taniko and skipped into the house.
“W-what was that all about?”
The female knight and Taniko walked over, tilting their heads in confusion.
“Lord Iwatani, Ren was acting strangely just now. Did he receive something nice?”
“Isn’t it just chocolate?”
“Well, yes, but…”
“I just thought there might be someone else besides us who’d be happy to get some.”

He said it as if it were the most natural thing in the world. If you knew that, you should’ve at least made him a single piece of chocolate! Even though there’s a slight chance he’s interested, these two really suck at handling special occasions.
“Ah, anticipating this might happen, I pretended to be you guys and dropped some chocolate in the mailbox for Ren.”
“What!?”
The female knight and Taniko openly showed their anger and confronted me. I think that’s a natural reaction. But with Ren, if I don’t do something like this, he just can’t stay motivated.

Just wait until tomorrow when he hasn’t received anything. It’ll be just like Christmas all over again. Then, when he sees someone like Itsuki eating chocolate, he’ll awaken to a curse born of jealousy. All while shouting something like, “I’ll blow up every happy couple!”
I need Ren to tackle the slave-hunting problem, after all. I’ve got to make sure he gets chocolate from a girl he likes and stays hyped up.
“What do you mean by that?!”
“Oh, come on, you guys know exactly how it feels to be the one who doesn’t get chocolate on Valentine’s Day, right?”
“How could I possibly know that?! What do you take me for, Lord Iwatani?!”
“Oh, right, you’re a girl. But today, you’re the one supposed to be receiving, aren’t you?”
“Ugh…”
The female knight’s voice caught slightly, as if she knew exactly what I was getting at. Taniko, too, was shooting me a disgusted look.
“I do admit there’s no day more annoying than today, though…”

A female knight who’s manly and dead serious. There’s no way she wouldn’t be popular. I guess even in another world, those standards don’t change. Well, since the Hero was the one who popularized them, I kind of saw that coming.
“Of all people, I actually sent Ren chocolate!? Did Lord Iwatani make it!?”
“Yeah, I put some chocolate—the kind you’d make, rough around the edges but clearly made with love—in a clumsy wrapper and dropped it in the mailbox.”
“Lord Iwatani! Did you toy with Ren’s heart!?”
“Hmph. I didn’t actually put your name on it, you know? I just made it look like something you’d send. Ren’s just mistakenly thinking it’s from you on his own.”
“Guh…”
“What about mine?”
“I didn’t put your name on that one either. I just used wrapping paper with a dragon brand and tucked a Gaelion scale into the ribbon. That way, Ren will mistake it for yours.”
She glared at me in silence. Stop giving me that look—it’s like the darkness of an abyss! Seriously, just make up your mind—do you hate me or like me? Or are you just curious about me?
“That’s the deal. If you’ve got some chocolate ready, go hand it over right now.”

The female knight brought the chocolate over with a look of utter disgust and showed it to me. It looked even worse than I’d imagined. Burnt to a crisp… Yeah, even the fake chocolate I made is better than this. Taniko’s is actually moving. Is it a chocolate monster or something?
But even before that, I’m surprised you were even making chocolate in the first place. If you have any, just give it to me. At worst, you could’ve just used Legendary Weapons to make it.
“Anyway, you guys better study hard before next year.”
“Guh… Lord Iwatani! I’m not going to let today’s incident slide!”
“I won’t forgive you.”

Hmph. Considering all the hostility you guys have shown me so far, that’s a pretty safe response. Anyway, you two actually like Ren quite a bit, don’t you? Either way, just get together already. Otherwise, Ren’s going to be a total pain in the neck.
Stop with that “neither too close nor too far” dynamic like in a shounen manga. It makes Ren unstable. Relationship instability is only acceptable in works of fiction.
“Do whatever you want. This is what happens when you don’t show up to a chocolate-making class in the village, even though she went to all that trouble to set it up.”
The female knight and Taniko walked away, looking bitter. I thought that would be the end of it, and the event would wrap up peacefully.
Yes—that’s when the Valentine’s Day nightmare began……
